title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1972-09-21
lineage: DAT (Tascam DA-40) > Tascam DA-3000 > Samplitude Pro X5 Suite > FLAC

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy night highlighted by a sweeping Dark Star, stellar Morning Dew, and crystal‑clear mix.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about this recording’s pristine soundboard quality – crisp, clear and virtually flawless aside from a tiny early scratch. Musically the show is a signature Dead performance with an epic Dark Star, powerful Morning Dew, and standout renditions of Sugar Magnolia, Bird Song and many classics, delivering consistently high energy throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: All three reviews are overwhelmingly positive; two give 5‑star ratings praising both the performance and the soundboard mix, while the third, despite a zero rating, offers no criticism. The show is described as a “signature night” with multiple standout jams, and the recording is called the best mix and crystal clear.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear sound with superb balance; reviewers call it the "best mix" and note only a slight scratch at the very start. Overall the tape is pristine and highly listenable.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows seamlessly, with a tight first set full of crisp renditions and an explosive second set that builds to an epic Dark Star climax before resolving into sweet jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Leads a beautiful spin on Morning Dew and drives the sweeping Dark Star jam; his tone is praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s vocal contributions are highlighted (Cumberland, intro style), showing strong presence in the performance.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocals receive high praise (“nails his vocal line”) and harmonies are noted on Jack Straw.
